summary: The change adds one line to the reader brief's reading rules. The line says that a behavior criterion for a loop (drain, queue), a protection, or rendered output must name the real path run end to end, its effect (item landed, record written) and a check that fails without it. It is marked `(prose only)` and comes after a Root cause comment that cites the three jobs. This follows the request's preference for giving the stage information over adding a refusal rule. A new unit test reads the brief and checks that it carries the rule. It passes now, and it would fail on the base code because its `.expect` needs a rendered `- Behavior:` line that the base does not have. No refusal check was added: refusal_corpus.rs is unchanged and its 24 tests pass, which fits the replay result of 0 of 50 readings newly refused. D184 and a CHANGELOG entry name the root cause, and D184 also covers the rejected alternatives and has a Provenance bullet. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed on this commit. Only minor issues remain: the rule line is shorter than criterion 1's wording (it leaves out "denial", "reported" and "page changed"), and an existing test comment was not updated after its size limit was raised.
